questions.prompt: What is the default TCP port a Redis server listens on?
questions.explanation: Redis listens on TCP port 6379 by default (5432 is PostgreSQL, 3306 is MySQL).

questions.prompt: How many logical databases does a Redis server expose by default, and how do you switch between them?

options.text: One database only; there is no switching

questions.explanation: By default there are 16 logical databases (0–15); SELECT changes the current one. They share the same server and config.

questions.prompt: Which statements about redis-cli and RESP are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Command names are case-insensitive (SET and set both work)
Replies are typed: simple strings, errors, integers, bulk strings, and arrays
You can run a single command like `redis-cli PING` without entering the interactive prompt

questions.explanation: Command names are case-insensitive and RESP replies are typed; you can pass a command as arguments to redis-cli. But KEYS are case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Why are the 16 logical databases a poor choice for isolating separate tenants?

options.text: They each require a separate license
They share the same server, memory, and configuration, and don't exist in Redis Cluster
They can only hold string values

questions.explanation: Logical databases are lightweight namespaces on one server — same memory and config, wiped together by FLUSHALL, and unsupported in Cluster. Use separate instances or key prefixes for isolation.

questions.prompt: The command that deletes every key in the CURRENT database only is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: FLUSHDB clears the current database; FLUSHALL clears all of them. Both are immediate and irreversible.

questions.prompt: Which command gives you a quick health check that the connection to Redis is working?
questions.explanation: PING returns PONG when the server is reachable and responsive. SAVE, SHUTDOWN, and FLUSHALL all have significant side effects.
